# publish_game_metadata_files

[← Command index](README.md)

Render the Pegasus metadata as one browsable HTML table per category.

## Synopsis

```
publish_game_metadata_files [options]
```

## Description

For each category, reads the metadata file of every subcategory that has one and
writes `Published/<Category>.html` in the game metadata repository, for example
`Nintendo.html`. Each game gets a table row with a per-platform number, its platform,
name, player count and co-op flag, and search links to GameFAQs and MobyGames.

Only `Roms` metadata is published. Existing pages are overwritten.

## Options

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Publish every category

```bash
publish_game_metadata_files
```

### Publish without the confirmation prompt

```bash
publish_game_metadata_files --no-preview
```

### Dry run

```bash
publish_game_metadata_files -p -v
```

## Notes

- There are no selection options; every category is published.
- `scan_game_files` runs this same step at the end of its pipeline.
